page_title: HardwareVisualizer – CPU & GPU Monitor with History

summary.name: HardwareVisualizer
summary.one_liner: A hardware monitor for Windows, macOS, and Linux that shows live CPU, GPU, temperature and process data and keeps history to review after heavy workloads.
use_cases: review CPU and GPU peaks after gaming
trace temperature rises during rendering or compiling
find which process used CPU or memory
compare current performance with earlier periods
monitor hardware on Windows, macOS or Linux
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a hardware monitor that shows CPU, GPU, temperature and process activity live. An Insights view lets you look back after a workload ends to see when CPU or GPU load peaked and how long it lasted. It plots temperature changes over time against CPU or GPU load. It includes sampled process activity to show which applications used CPU or memory. You can return to an earlier period and compare the same metrics with the current ones. History is kept for 30 days by default and retention is configurable.
notable: Insights view for reviewing load and temperature after gaming or heavy tasks
Temperature changes correlated with CPU or GPU load over time
Sampled per-process CPU and memory attribution
History retained 30 days by default, configurable
caveats: Pricing and licensing are not stated on the page
Process data is sampled rather than continuous
Listing is under a macOS apps list but the page names Windows and Linux too
